d.d: Stimulating to the senses; engaging; charming.
Favorably stimulating to the palate; pleasantly spicy; tangy.
Producing a burning sensation due to the presence of chilies or similar spices; spicy, hot.
To wound the pride of (someone); to excite to anger; to irritate, to offend.
To excite (someone) to action, especially by causing jealousy, resentment, etc.; also, to stimulate (an emotion or feeling, especially curiosity or interest).
d.x: I believe this will pique your interest.

d.d: Enmity, ill feeling (uncountable); a feeling of animosity or a dispute (countable).

Irritation or resentment awakened by a social injury or slight; offence, especially taken in an emotional sense with little consideration or thought (uncountable); or especially in fit of pique: a transient feeling of wounded pride (countable).
In piquet, the right of the elder hand to count thirty in hand, or to play before the adversary counts one.
simple past and past participle of pique
Annoyed, usually mildly and temporarily, especially by an offense to one's pride or honor.
third-person singular simple present indicative of pique
A game of cards for two people, with thirty-two cards, all the deuces, threes, fours, fives, and sixes being set aside.
A kind of corded or ribbed fabric made from cotton, rayon, or silk.
A movement in which the raised, pointed foot of the working leg is lowered so that it pricks the floor and then either rebounds upward or becomes a supporting foot.
